# General Purposes {#PurposeSection}

These guidelines compile the minimum data standards and recommended practices for the management and reporting of at-sea observation data collected under the IOTC Regional Observer Scheme (ROS) by onboard observers and Electronic Monitoring Systems (EMS). They aim to promote the consistency, completeness and quality of ROS data submitted to the Secretariat of the Indian Ocean Tuna Commission (IOTC), in accordance with the reporting obligations established under the ROS and relevant [IOTC Conservation and Management Measures](https://iotc.org/cmms) (CMMs).

These guidelines are intended as a reference for [IOTC Contracting Parties and Cooperating Non-Contracting Parties](https://iotc.org/about-iotc/structure-commission) (CPCs) when preparing and submitting ROS data to the IOTC Secretariat.

## Scope

The ROS was established to collect verified catch data and other scientific data related to fisheries for tuna and tuna-like species in the IOTC Area of Competence, as defined in the IOTC Agreement.

These guidelines apply to ROS data collected from vessels subject to the requirements of the Scheme, including vessels of 24 metres length overall and above, and vessels under 24 metres length overall when operating outside their exclusive economic zone (EEZ).

CPCs are responsible for ensuring that vessels flying their flag conduct fishing operations in accordance with applicable IOTC CMMs. As part of these obligations, CPCs must ensure that the required level of observer coverage specified in the applicable IOTC ROS CMM is achieved, and that data collected by onboard observers and EMS are reported to the IOTC Secretariat in accordance with the data standards endorsed by the Scientific Committee. In the event of any inconsistency between these guidelines and an applicable IOTC CMM, the provisions of the CMM shall prevail.

Observer programmes are established and managed by CPCs, which are responsible for the recruitment, training, certification, deployment, and oversight of observers, in accordance with the [IOTC ROS Standards](https://iotc.org/sites/default/files/documents/ROS/Standards/IOTC_Regional_Observer_Scheme_Standards.pdf). CPCs are responsible for ensuring that observer data are submitted in accordance with the agreed [ROS Data Standards](https://iotc.org/sites/default/files/documents/ROS/Standards/Data_standard_ROS_fields.xlsx).

CPCs implementing EMS are responsible for the installation, operation, maintenance, and management of their EMS programmes and must ensure that their electronic monitoring frameworks comply with the standards and requirements established under the IOTC Regional Electronic Monitoring Programme (REMP), including applicable technical specifications, data collection protocols and data review procedures ([ROS EMS Programme Standards](https://iotc.org/sites/default/files/documents/ROS/Standards/Electronic_monitoring_program_standards.pdf)). CPCs are also responsible for ensuring that EMS-derived data are reviewed, validated and reported to the IOTC Secretariat in accordance with the applicable [EMS System and Data Standards](https://iotc.org/sites/default/files/documents/ROS/Standards/Electronic_monitoring_system_and_data_standards.pdf).

While the principal requirements of the ROS are established through the relevant ROS CMM, other IOTC CMMs may establish additional or species-specific data collection and reporting requirements applicable when observers are onboard or EMS are deployed. The IOTC Secretariat periodically reviews these CMMs to ensure that applicable reporting requirements are appropriately reflected in the ROS reporting forms.
